title: Hotel booking and date overlaps
idea: A hotel booking design finds a room of the requested type whose existing stays do not overlap the new dates, then claims it in one locked step.
points: Core entities: `Room`, a room `Type`, a `Stay` date range, `Reservation` and `ReservationService`.
A `Stay` is half-open: the check-out day is free for the next guest.
Two stays overlap when each one starts before the other ends.
The overlap check and the insert must run under one lock, ideally per room.

hero.title: Two guests, one last room

left.title: Check, then book (racy)
items: Thread A sees room 101 free for 10 to 13 March
Thread B checks before A saves, and also sees it free
Both add a reservation: the room is double booked
Tests usually pass because the bad timing is rare

right.title: Check and book as one step
items: Each room has its own lock object
Overlap check and insert run inside that lock
B waits for the lock, then sees A's stay and is refused
Bookings for other rooms never wait on room 101

hero.verdict: Correctness comes from making check-and-insert atomic; a lock per room keeps it fast.

code.title: Searching by type and dates
code.caption: Four guests ask for a double room. Back-to-back stays share a room; overlapping ones do not.

walk.text: `Stay` rejects empty ranges in its compact constructor and owns the overlap rule.
Pick rooms of the type, then drop any room with an overlapping reservation.
Take and record the first free room. One `synchronized` method is simple but global; `RaceDemo` locks per room.
Ana leaves on the 13th, so Cy can arrive that day. Dee overlaps both rooms.

code.title: Eight threads, one room
code.caption: A latch releases eight threads at once. The per-room lock lets exactly one win.

walk.text: Every task waits on the latch, so all eight try to book together.
Open the latch, then wait for the pool to finish before printing.
One list per room, created safely by `ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent`.
The room's list is its lock. Checking and adding happen in one block.
Room 102 has its own list and lock, so the race on 101 left it free.

pitfalls: Do not treat the check-out date as booked; use half-open ranges or back-to-back stays fail.
Never check availability and insert in separate steps without a lock or database constraint.
Avoid one global lock for the whole hotel when a lock per room is enough.

quiz.why: Dee's 11 to 14 March overlaps Ana in 101 and Ben in 102. Room 201 is a suite, so it is filtered out by type.

takeaway: Half-open date ranges for overlap; one lock per room for check-and-insert.

starters: How would this work with a database instead of in-memory lists?
How do I hold a room for ten minutes while the guest pays?
Should I store availability per night instead of a list of stays?
